title: WSEvent
description:
One message on the WebSocket connection between the app and its clients.

`WSEvent` is the app's whole live protocol. The embedded server pushes game state out to the
browser player client and the external display, and those clients send edits back, all as
events carrying a `name` and a `data` payload.

The payload is deliberately untyped (`Any?`) because its shape depends entirely on the name —
a `tokenUpdated` carries a `Token`, a `tokenMoved` carries a `Movement`, a `messageCreated`
carries a `Message`. The `Codable` conformance is hand-written for exactly this reason:
`init(from:)` switches on the name to decode the right type, and `encode(to:)` switches
again to encode it.

Events pair into requests and responses through `requestId` and `responseId`, so a client
asking a question — `getAttribute`, say — can match the answer to its question.

- SeeAlso: `Game`, `Map`, `Token`, `Message`

name.description:
What this event reports or requests.

Determines how `data` is interpreted.

data.description:
The event's payload.

Untyped because its shape depends on `name`; the coding methods narrow it.

requestId.description:
The sender's correlation identifier, set on an incoming request.

The app echoes it back as the reply's `responseId`.

responseId.description:
The identifier of the request this event answers.

`nil` for events broadcast on the app's own initiative rather than in reply to anything.

Name.title: Name
Name.description:
What a `WSEvent` reports or requests.

The name determines the payload type — see the discussion on `WSEvent`. Names ending in
`-Updated`, `-Created` and `-Deleted` are the app broadcasting a change; names in the
imperative (`createEntity`, `updateDoor`) are a client asking for one.

Source.title: Source
Source.description: Who originated an action, for attributing it back to a client.

color.description: The client's accent color, as an RGB string.

Movement.title: Movement
Movement.description:
A drag in progress on a map object.

- SeeAlso: `ControlState`

id.description: The identifier of the object being moved.

x.description: The object's horizontal position in map coordinates.

y.description: The object's vertical position in map coordinates.

state.description: The phase of the drag — whether this is a live update or the final position.

polygon.description: The token's visible area at this position, when line of sight is enabled.

path.description: The route taken so far, as a flat list of alternating coordinates.

distance.description:
The distance travelled, formatted for display.

## Examples
- `"30 ft"`

animated.description: Whether the receiver should animate to the new position rather than jump to it.

source.description: The client that initiated the drag.

Frame.title: Frame
Frame.description: A viewport position on a map.

x.description: The horizontal center of the viewport in map coordinates.

y.description: The vertical center of the viewport in map coordinates.

Image.title: Image
Image.description: An updated image for a map, such as a redrawn fog-of-war mask.

id.description: The identifier of the map the image belongs to.

image.description: The image itself, encoded for transport.

VideoControl.title: VideoControl
VideoControl.description:
Playback state for a map's background video.

Lets every display stay in sync on an animated map.

Focus.title: Focus
Focus.description: A request to draw the players' attention to a point on the map.

x.description: The horizontal position in map coordinates.

y.description: The vertical position in map coordinates.

color.description: The highlight color, as an RGB string.

effect.description: Whether to play the attention-drawing animation.

pan.description: Whether to pan the viewport to the point.

zoom.description: Whether to zoom in on the point.

reset.description: Whether to restore the previous viewport instead of moving to the point.

Door.title: Door
Door.description:
A request to change a door's state.

Opening a door changes what the party can see, so this is applied to the wall mesh and the
resulting vision is rebroadcast.

- SeeAlso: `Wall/DoorState`

mapId.description: The identifier of the map the door is on.

id.description: The identifier of the wall acting as the door.

Attribute.title: Attribute
Attribute.description: A request to read or write an entity's attributes.

entityId.description: The identifier of the entity to read from or write to.

attributes.description: The attributes to write, or the attributes read back in the reply.
